newsitem.title: USA: J.P. Morgan extends benefits to same-sex partners.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan extends benefits to same-sex partners.

text.p: J.P. Morgan & Co. Inc. has extended medical and dental benefits to the same-sex partners of its employees.
A spokesman for the company Thursday confirmed the policy change, which was described in a memo to employees that said J.P. Morgan was the first Wall Street firm to offer such benefits.
According to the memo, same-sex partners will be eligible for the benefits beginning Dec. 1.

"Since same-sex couples cannot legally marry, under our current rules employees in these nontraditional families can't protect each other from unanticipated medical expenses," the memo said. It added that the change only affected U.S. plans while the company reviews laws and practices that would affect employees in other countries.
The spokesman said the change did not extend to opposite-sex domestic partners since those individuals have the option of entering into a legal marriage.

The memo said the company believes the change will affect only a small number of employees and have minimal efect on costs. The memo, issued by the human resources department, said the new policy will enhance the company's reputation as an attractive employer to those who value diversity.
